title: The Twelve Dancing Princesses
summary: Twelve lovely princesses slept in twelve beds in a locked royal chamber, yet every morning their slippers were found worn into holes as if they had danced all night!...
keywords: the twelve dancing princesses (die zertanzten schuhe)
full_text:
Twelve lovely princesses slept in twelve beds in a locked royal chamber, yet every morning their slippers were found worn into holes as if they had danced all night!

The king promised his kingdom to whoever could solve the mystery in three nights; failure meant the scaffold. Many princes tried, fell into drugged slumber, and were executed.

An old wounded soldier received an invisible cloak from an old woman: "Do not drink the wine they offer you, and pretend to sleep!"

The soldier feigned sleep. At midnight, the eldest princess tapped her bed; it sank into the earth, opening a secret stair. Putting on his invisible cloak, the soldier followed them down through groves of silver trees, gold trees, and diamond trees, breaking a twig from each.

They crossed a subterranean lake in twelve boats rowed by twelve handsome princes, entering an enchanted golden castle where they danced until their satin shoes were shredded!

On the third morning, the soldier stood before the king, showed the silver, gold, and diamond twigs, and produced the golden goblet he had taken.

The princesses confessed the enchantment; the soldier chose the eldest princess as his bride and inherited the crown.
moral: Vigilance, discretion, and presence of mind solve the deepest enchantments.
